A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Differentially Private Clustered Federated Learning. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–J are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained figures across renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification accuracy, cluster-detection and sensitivity results on MNIST, FMNIST and CIFAR10 in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experiments and adds an empirical study of EM iteration counts in Appendix F, Figure 13.

M1.justification: The full-batch first round, GMM soft clustering and subsequent private local model selection are retained. Adding 'private' to Algorithm 1's clustering comment clarifies the procedure already documented in v2 Appendices C.3 and D.6.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST and FMNIST with rotation shifts, and CIFAR10 with rotation and label shifts, retaining minority-cluster and local-dataset-size scenarios. The new EM experiment uses the existing CIFAR10 covariate-shift setting with four clusters.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain Global, Local, private IFCA, MR-MTL and oracle O-DPCFL. Global already appears in v2 Figures 10–11; no corresponding comparison gains or loses a baseline.

E3.justification: New Figure 13 measures EM iterations while varying first-round batch size from Ni/16 to Ni, with Ni=10000 and privacy budgets 4 and 5. This adds a computational evaluation protocol; the existing classification splits, models and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 studies batch-size effects on noise and cluster separation and presents EM convergence theory. v6 adds a direct sensitivity analysis of EM fitting iterations versus first-round batch size in Figure 13, empirically examining the claimed computational benefit.

E5.justification: Four-run reporting and shaded accuracy bands in Figures 4–5 and 10–11, and five data-split seeds in Figure 9, are retained. New Figure 13 introduces no stated run-count, seed or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Figure 13 newly reports roughly 80–100 EM iterations at Ni/16 and about three at full batch for privacy budgets 4 and 5. v2 has no corresponding iteration-count results. Existing accuracy and cluster-recovery results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds an explicit adaptive composition proposition with unequal RDP budgets summing to epsilon1+epsilon2; v2 stated the equal-budget E-epsilon rule and discussed heterogeneous composition informally. The added Gaussian-mechanism proposition largely restates the bound already used in v2 G.4. Central lemmas, the EM theorem and proof calculations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of robust private clustering, benefits from large initial batches, efficient GMM fitting and improved utility under structured heterogeneity. The added EM experiment supports an existing contribution rather than introducing a new central claim.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations and qualifications concerning local dataset size are retained. Figure 13 supports the interpretation already given in Section 4.3. Removing cross-device FL as an example of future scarce-data settings does not change the stated applicability boundary.

D1.justification: Appendices D–E and I retain data processing, model specifications, hyperparameter grids, privacy accounting, GMM implementation settings and gradient-accumulation guidance. The added initialization citations do not change implementation or resource-access information.

R1.justification: Appendix D.8 adds Arthur and Vassilvitskii (2007) and Biernacki et al. (2003) to support GMM initialization choices. Related-work Sections 2 and J and the positioning against previous DPFL approaches remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v6 makes localized wording and grammar edits, shortens Algorithm 1 comments, explicitly explains the approximation symbol, revises Appendix F's heading and narrative, and corrects an algorithm-line reference. The overall organization and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v6 adds Figure 13 and reflows Appendix F, renumbering old Figures 13–14 as 14–15. It also corrects swapped first-round and later-round batch-size labels in the noise-scale plot's annotations; the plotted surface and numerical noise-scale values are unchanged.

improvement.justification: New Figure 13 provides limited empirical support for a computational-efficiency claim that v2 supported theoretically. Corrected plot annotations and more explicit privacy background also improve clarity and checkability. These are modest gains: the central method and benchmark results are unchanged, and the new experiment adds no uncertainty reporting.
